newsitem.title: FRANCE: French credit demand rose 10.6 pct in first half.
newsitem.headline: French credit demand rose 10.6 pct in first half.

text.p: New lending from French specialist credit institutions rose 10.6 percent in the first half of the year versus a year ago, totalling 141 billion francs, figures from the ASF French association for finance houses showed on Thursday.
The new lending figures were up 5.7 percent from the 1995 second half.

Demand was more evenly distributed than previous six month periods, with company borrowing for new equipment and household credit showing the largest increase, up 12.3 percent from first-half 1995, to 108.4 billion francs, while property lending rose 5.2 percent to 32.6 billion francs.

Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet told a parliamentary finance committee meeting on Wednesday that one could expect a recovery in lending, due largely to a rise in housing loans, according to minutes of the meeting released on Thursday.
He said the solvability of householders had been significantly improved, mainly due to a fall in long-term interest rates, the minutes said.
